beginner.headline: Thousands Protest Over Cost of Living in France
beginner.brief: More than half a million people protested in France. They are angry about the high cost of living. Many students also protested because their schools need more teachers. Most people marched peacefully during the afternoon. Later in the day, some groups started fires in the streets. Police arrested more than 1,200 people because of the violence. The government promised to find extra teachers to help the schools.

intermediate.headline: Violence and Arrests Across France During Nationwide Demonstrations
intermediate.brief: Violence broke out across France on Saturday during demonstrations against hardship in schools and financial difficulties. In Paris, there were significant clashes into the evening with riot police, who used tear gas to control crowds. Widespread vandalism targeted businesses, and looting was reported in several major cities. As the day continued, some groups torched vehicles in the city streets. Local police said hostile individuals prevented firefighters from safely tackling the blaze. Hundreds of thousands of students have also demonstrated recently over staff shortages and poor facilities in secondary schools. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that 150 police officers were injured in the unrest. Meanwhile, Macron promised that individuals who attacked public buildings would be prosecuted.

advanced.headline: Violent Demonstrations Erupt Across France Amid Economic Pressures
advanced.brief: Widespread disorder erupted across France as more than half a million people joined demonstrations against economic pressures. The government characterised the disturbances as an escalation in violence, detaining at least 1,200 individuals who had taken to the streets. In Paris, significant confrontations occurred into the evening, prompting riot police to deploy tear gas and water cannon against the crowds. As the day wore on, some factions ignited fires in the street and torched vehicles in iconic central locations. Emergency crews also battled flames at the Limoges town hall, which the local prefecture confirmed caused part of the building to collapse. Furthermore, a historic tourist office was burnt in Lyon, a destruction the local mayor described as a tragedy. Hundreds of thousands of students have recently mobilised against inadequate staffing and dilapidated facilities in secondary schools. Their numbers have been bolstered by the prominent yellow vest movement and other demonstrating groups. This latest wave of turbulence arrives as France enters a period of deep political uncertainty. Consequently, the government has made apparent attempts at concessions, with the education minister pledging 3,000 additional supply teachers.
